subject: Day 26: post-visit follow-through; first cooing sounds
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 26. If the 1-month visit was earlier this week, follow through on what the pediatrician flagged. Vowel sounds (ah, ooh) are emerging during awake-alert windows.

Action items
- Act on anything the pediatrician flagged at the 1-month visit (latch correction, supplementation pattern, vitamin D dosing). AAP HealthyChildren on vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Confirm vitamin D 400 IU/day is in place if breastfeeding exclusively or predominantly. AAP HealthyChildren on vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Schedule the 2-month well visit if it is not already booked (target day 56-70). AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- If returning to work soon, confirm daycare or nanny start date matches the return date with a 1-2 week buffer. ChildCare.gov directory: https://www.childcare.gov/
- Continue the feeding log.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] First vowel coos (ah, ooh); social smiles; sustained eye contact.
- [low concern] Cradle cap; blocked tear duct without redness.
- [monitor] Crying more than three hours a day on more than three days a week; colic peaks at six to eight weeks.
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting with weight loss. Persistent inability to console with back-arching during feeds.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Take conversational turns with each vocalization — respond, pause, respond again. Turn-taking is the foundational language pattern. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Face-to-face talking with exaggerated expressions during alert windows.
- Tummy time near 20 minutes a day across short bouts. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Read aloud the same three to five board books on rotation; repetition supports rhythm recognition.

Upcoming
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window (if not yet done).
- Day 35-42: peak-crying curve.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; first round of vaccines.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Calms when picked up or spoken to
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Early co-regulation. Not the same as stopping crying immediately — look for any shift in state.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/calms-with-soothing/complete

- Briefly lifts head during tummy time
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Few seconds of head lift, even with bobble, counts. Builds neck strength for later head control.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brief-head-lift/complete

- Quiets or turns toward a familiar voice
  AAP window: day 7-45
  What to look for: Voice recognition begins before birth; postnatally it shows as orienting or settling to a parent's voice.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/recognizes-parent-voice/complete

- Watches your face when you talk
  AAP window: day 7-60
  What to look for: Baseline social orientation. Look for sustained gaze, even briefly, during alert windows.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-face-briefly/complete

- Moves both arms and both legs
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-arms-and-legs/complete
